items.howItWorks: Antifungal treats skin fungal and yeast infections
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for dermatophyte skin fungal infections (tinea pedis, tinea cruris (jock itch), tinea corporis) caused by dermatophytes, and for tinea versicolor and cutaneous candidiasis caused by Pityrosporum orbiculare.
items.usage: Apply to the affected area (diseased site) 1 to 2 times a day. The treatment period depending on the disease: for tinea pedis (athlete's foot), once a day for 1 week; for interdigital (between the toes) type tinea pedis (athlete's foot), twice a day for 1 week; for plantar (sole) type tinea pedis (athlete's foot), twice a day for 2 weeks; for tinea corporis and tinea cruris (jock itch), 1 to 2 weeks; for cutaneous candidiasis, 1 to 2 weeks; for tinea versicolor, use for 2 weeks.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, nursing mothers, and children must not use this medicine. Unless directed by a physician, do not use occlusive dressing or wrapping methods. In the case of candidiasis, do not use acidic soap. Use this medicine for external application only. Do not use it ophthalmically on the cornea or conjunctiva; if it accidentally gets into the eyes, this medicine may irritate the eyes and, rarely, may worsen a latent fungal (mold) infection, so wash it out completely with plenty of water. Do not use on the nails, scalp, around the mouth, or the vaginal area. If symptoms do not improve even after the treatment period, consult a physician or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If hypersensitivity reactions accompanied by rash, excessive irritation, skin hives, redness, rash, erythema, itching, a sensation of irritation, localized contact dermatitis, skin peeling, wound scabbing, pigmentation abnormalities, stinging pain, burning sensation, etc. occur, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of joints and muscles
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesia and anti-inflammation of degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis/tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, humeral epicondylitis (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain (myositis, fasciitis, etc.), and post-traumatic swelling/pain.
items.usage: For adults, apply a thin layer of about 3 cm (1 g) per dose to the affected area 3 to 4 times a day and rub gently so that it is well absorbed.
items.precaution:
Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or piroxicam preparations, patients with or those who have experienced aspirin asthma (asthma attacks caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.), children 14 years of age or younger, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and nursing mothers must not use this medicine.

Before using this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma, the elderly, and patients with or those who have experienced hypersensitivity to propylene glycol should consult a physician or pharmacist.

Do not use on lesioned skin (hemorrhagic skin disease, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds), eyes, or mucous membrane areas.

Do not use the occlusive dressing method.
items.adverse: If occasionally localized itching, redness, rash, scaling, eczema/dermatitis, contact dermatitis, erythema, or rarely photosensitivity, etc. occur, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of joints and muscles
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesia and anti-inflammation of degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis (tendon inflammation)/tenosynovitis (tendon sheath inflammation), peritendinitis (tendon), humeral (upper arm bone) epicondylitis (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and post-traumatic swelling/pain (swelling/pain after injury).
items.usage: After removing the release liner from the medicated surface, attach to the affected area (diseased site) once a day.
items.precaution: This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity and photosensitivity to this medicine, patients with or those who have experienced aspirin asthma (asthma attacks caused by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, etc.), patients with hypersensitivity to ingredients that may cause cross-hypersensitivity reactions (tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate, oxybenzone), pregnant women 6 months or more into pregnancy, children under 15 years of age, and on the eyes, mucous membranes, athlete's foot, or tinea. Before using this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma, pregnant women or nursing mothers, and use on damaged skin, eczema, or rash areas should be discussed with a physician or pharmacist. While using this medicine and for up to 2 weeks after use, regardless of the weather, avoid outdoor activities, and when going out in daily life, cover the applied area of this medicine with clothing, sunglasses, a hat, sunscreen, etc. so as not to be exposed to ultraviolet rays. Do not use the occlusive dressing method. If no improvement in symptoms is seen even after using for about 1 week, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If, rarely, shock, anaphylactoid symptoms (hives, difficulty breathing, facial swelling and other hypersensitivity-like symptoms), asthma attacks (dry rales (bubbling sounds), wheezing (whistling breath), difficulty breathing), or occasionally contact dermatitis such as redness (congested and reddened), rash, itching, blisters, sores, sensation of irritation and swelling (swelling), skin dryness and pigmentation, etc. occur, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of veins and injuries
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesia and anti-inflammation of varicose edema, superficial phlebitis, accidental trauma, sports injury (bruises), and tenosynovitis.
items.usage: Apply a thin layer to the wounded or infected area several times a day, then rub the skin gently.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or salicylates, patients 4 weeks before the delivery date, must not use this medicine on mucous membrane areas or open wound areas. Before using this medicine, newborns and children, patients with renal (kidney) failure, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and nursing mothers should consult a physician or pharmacist. Follow the prescribed dosage and administration well. Be careful not to let it get into the eyes and do not apply over too wide an area. Use for external application only. When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
items.adverse: If, rarely, dermatitis, contact allergy, tinnitus (ringing in the ears) accompanied by hearing impairment, nosebleed, nausea, vomiting, itching, and dryness of the skin and mucous membranes, etc. occur, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.
items.interaction: When used together with other anticoagulants (e.g., coumarin, aspirin, dipyridamole, dextran, streptokinase, etc.), bleeding may increase, so consult a physician or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves pain and inflammation of joints and muscles
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesia and anti-inflammation of degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis/tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, humeral epicondylitis (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and post-traumatic swelling/pain.
items.usage: Depending on the symptoms, apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 4 times a day and rub gently so that it is well absorbed.
items.precaution: Patients with hypersensitivity or photosensitivity to this medicine, patients who have experienced asthma caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients with hypersensitivity to tiaprofenic acid, fenofibrate, bezafibrate, ciprofibrate, or oxybenzone, pregnant women 6 months or more into pregnancy, and children under 15 years of age must not use this medicine. Before using this medicine, patients with bronchial asthma, pregnant women, and nursing mothers should consult a physician or pharmacist. Because photosensitivity may occur, avoid ultraviolet rays while using this medicine and for up to 2 weeks after use. Do not use on the eyes, mucous membranes, athlete's foot, or tinea. When used on damaged skin and mucous membranes, eczema, or rash areas, it may cause temporary irritation and sharp pain, so use with caution. Do not use the occlusive dressing method. If no improvement in symptoms is seen even after using for about 1 week, stop use and consult a physician or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If, rarely, shock symptoms (hives, difficulty breathing, facial swelling and other hypersensitivity-like symptoms), asthma attacks (dry rales, wheezing, difficulty breathing), or occasionally contact dermatitis such as redness, rash, itching, blisters, sores, sensation of irritation and swelling, skin dryness and pigmentation, photosensitivity caused by direct sunlight occur, or if the skin rash spreads to the whole body, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Antifungal treats athlete's foot and tinea
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for athlete's foot, tinea cruris (jock itch), and tinea corporis.
items.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the diseased area once a day.
items.precaution:
Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, infants 2 years of age or younger, must not use this medicine on the eyes or around the eyes, mucous membranes (e.g., inside the mouth, inside the nose, vagina, etc.), the genital area, the external genitalia, eczema, moist areas, sores, cracks, or severely wounded diseased areas.

Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and nursing mothers, infants and children, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines, persons whose diseased area is on the face or is extensive or festering, persons for whom the distinction between eczema and athlete's foot/tinea cruris (jock itch) or tinea corporis is unclear, and asthma patients should consult a physician or pharmacist.

Follow the prescribed dosage and administration well.

When administering to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Use this medicine for external application only and do not use it internally.

Use after cleaning the diseased area and its surroundings.

Do not touch the eyes or mucous membranes with hands that have this medicine on them.

Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, immediately wash it out with water or warm water.

If there is no improvement in symptoms even after using for about 2 weeks, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.
items.adverse: If rash and reddening from congestion, itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer, etc., edema (swelling), sensation of irritation, scaling, sores, blisters, cracking, etc. occur, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.

items.howItWorks: Relieves gum, mouth, and tongue inflammation
items.efficacy: This medicine is used for the relief of chronic desquamative gingivitis, and intractable stomatitis and glossitis accompanied by erosion or ulcers.
items.usage:
Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area once to several times a day.

Adjust appropriately by increasing or decreasing according to age and symptoms.
items.precaution:
Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or those who have experienced it, patients with tuberculous, viral, or other purulent infections in the oral cavity, patients with syphilis, chickenpox, mycosis, bacterial skin infection, perioral dermatitis, rosacea, or gingivitis caused by vitamin C deficiency must not use this medicine.

Before using this medicine, pregnant women, infants and children, and the elderly should consult a physician or pharmacist.

Do not eat food immediately after use.

Do not use this medicine ophthalmically.
items.adverse:
If oral infection (fungal and bacterial infections in the oral cavity) occurs, stop use immediately and consult a physician or pharmacist.

A numb sensation in the oral cavity, taste abnormalities or reduction, and rarely allergic reactions may occur.
